title: delta-bank-timeline-comm-draft
content:
PURPOSE:
Quick personal scratchpad for Delta Bank (priv deployment) outage on 2025-11-04 -> draft of internal timeline + short comm to customer. Informal — notes to self, commands tried, raw errors, hypotheses. DO NOT SHARE AS-IS.

SUMMARY (one-line):
- Traffic started 09:03 UTC: gradual increase in 503s from routing layer, full service disruption by 09:18 UTC. Primary correlation to model-serving pool OOM events + control-plane rollouts.

RAW TIMELINE (local times UTC):
- 2025-11-04 08:56 — routine canary deploy started (control plane): config-rollout/route-policy v12 -> v13 (automated).
- 2025-11-04 09:02 — first alert from Delta monitoring: increase in 5xx on /v1/generate (client-side). 09:02–09:06 spikes intermittent ~5–10% errors.
- 2025-11-04 09:07 — internal SRE pager: increased latency + 503s from gateway.
- 2025-11-04 09:12 — autoscaler started adding nodes but several pods show CrashLoopBackOff with OOMKilled.
- 2025-11-04 09:18 — most requests to Delta's dedicated pool return 503. Traffic routed to fallback models for some customers but Delta has strict routing/pinning so fallback blocked -> outage persists.
- 2025-11-04 09:30 — mitigation attempt 1: revert route-policy v13 -> v12 (control plane) — partial improvement but errors persisted for pinned sessions.
- 2025-11-04 09:45 — mitigation attempt 2: increase GPU instance pool by +30% (manual) — new nodes joined but with older driver causing some pods to fail driver init.
- 2025-11-04 10:05 — final: pinned sessions gradually recovered after manual reschedule to healthy nodes and kv-cache warm-up; postmortem window starts.

COMMANDS/TRACES I RAN (raw):
- kubectl -n delta get pods --show-labels | grep serving
  -> many pods: model-serving-xx-3  CrashLoopBackOff  OOMKilled (exitCode 137)

- kubectl -n delta logs model-serving-xx-3 --previous
  -> "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 2048MiB (GPU 0)"
  -> also "Failed to allocate kv cache segment: insufficient memory"

- kubectl -n delta describe pod model-serving-xx-3
  -> Events: Back-off restarting failed container; kubelet eviction threshold triggered; memory.available below eviction.

- docker logs runtime-agent | grep "nv_peer_alloc"
  -> "nv_peer_alloc failed: -9" (repeated)

- curl -v https://priv.delta.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
  -> * Connected to priv.delta.example.com (10.1.2.3) port 443
  -> < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  -> {"error":"service_unavailable","message":"no healthy replicas for model: fast-ggml-quant"}

- tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.1.2.3 and port 443 -w /tmp/delta-cap.pcap (sniff showed TLS handshakes succeeded but backend responded 503).

- journalctl -u route-manager | tail -n 500
  -> "policy v13 applied"
  -> "route selection: eligible replicas 0 for pool delta-dedicated:fast-ggml-quant"

ERROR SNIPPETS (cut/paste):
- "ERROR: model_evaluator: failed to reserve KV cache slot: OutOfMemoryError"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 2048MiB (GPU 0)"
- "service_unavailable: no healthy replicas for model: fast-ggml-quant"
- "kubelet eviction threshold reached: memory.available=123Mi below threshold=200Mi"

HYPOTHESES (ordered by likelihood):
1) Memory pressure on dedicated pool (KV cache + model footprints) + new config (v13) increased concurrency per-replica -> OOMs -> pods killed -> route-manager sees 0 healthy replicas -> 503s.
2) Config v13 changed routing/weighting so more traffic pinned to a smaller set of replicas (unintended hot-shard) causing imbalance.
3) A subset of new nodes had mismatched GPU drivers (seen during manual scale up) causing some pods to fail GPU initialization -> unavailable replicas.
4) KV-cache invalidation bug in runtime: after deploy, existing sessions attempted to rehydrate caches and exceeded memory budget (seen in kv-cache allocation errors).
5) Networking flakiness was secondary (TLS handshakes OK); not primary cause.

QUICK MITIGATIONS WE DID (notes):
- Reverted route-policy v13 -> v12 at 09:30. (helped median latency for non-pinned traffic)
- Manual scale-up + node drain/reschedule to healthy nodes (10:00) -> recovered majority of pinned sessions after rewarm.
- Raised OOM alert thresholds and added temporary per-pod memory limit increase for delta pool (workaround).

CUSTOMER-FACING DRAFT (short) — for review by CS lead:
Subject: Brief outage summary and next steps (Delta Bank)
Hi Sam (Delta team),
We’re sorry for the disruption you experienced earlier today. Brief summary: between 09:02–09:40 UTC on 2025-11-04 some requests to your dedicated inference pool returned 503 due to insufficient capacity in the model-serving layer after an internal routing config change. We reverted the configuration and rescheduled workloads to healthy nodes; services recovered by ~10:05 UTC.
What happened: a combination of increased concurrency from a config rollout and memory pressure in the dedicated pool caused several model replicas to OOM, reducing the available pool to 0 for the pinned model.
What we did: reverted rollout, added capacity, rescheduled pods to healthy GPU nodes, increased per-pod memory limits temporarily, and warmed KV caches.
Immediate next steps we will take for Delta (ETA + owner):
- run a postmortem and publish RCA (target 2025-11-10) — owner: Priya
- add a safety cap in route-manager to avoid hot-shard pinning (ETA 2025-11-07) — owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime
- validate node driver compatibility during autoscaling (ETA 2025-11-09) — owner: Infra
- propose conservative config gating for route-policy rollouts to prevent sudden concurrency changes (ETA 2025-11-12) — owner: Product/Console

Draft apology line (short):
We sincerely apologize for the disruption and the impact on your users; we’re treating this as high priority and will share a full RCA by 2025-11-10.

NOTES-TO-SELF / OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Need to capture exact kernel driver versions for nodes that failed GPU init: ask infra for node autoscaler logs and image/driver manifest.
- Verify whether pinned sessions map to older kv-cache format (possible mismatch after runtime upgrade).
- Reproduce locally: simulate kv-cache rehydrate + high concurrency on a small pool -> see OOM behavior.
- Check if route-manager rollout v13 change is in PR history (who approved?) -> link to PR in linked_artifacts.
- Should we add explicit capacity health check that signals route-manager to not send traffic to pool if available_memory < X?

FOLLOWUPS (next actions):
- 2025-11-05 09:00 — sync with Infra (Zara) to get node driver list + autoscaler events.
- 2025-11-05 11:00 — run isolated repro in staging with kv-cache rehydrate (assign to Ethan).
- 2025-11-06 15:00 — draft RCA doc (Priya) and share with CS + Eng for review.

RANDOM NOTES / WORKING THOUGHTS (unpolished):
- If KV cache rehydrate is the keel, then maybe we need a background-slow-warmup strategy instead of all-at-once; could throttle rehydrate per-session.
- Consider an immediate hotfix: route-manager should prefer distributing pinned sessions across more distinct replicas (if possible) when memory pressure observed.
- Keep customer communication short, then append detailed RCA later.

END OF SCRATCHPAD
